public_brief: Our signup form takes phone numbers as free text, and people type them every which way: dashes, dots, parentheses, stray country prefixes, extensions, odd spacing. Implement normalize_phone(raw), which takes one raw string exactly as typed and returns a cleaned, canonical string the CRM can store. Input you cannot confidently clean needs a defined outcome too - decide whether that means raising an exception or returning something obviously unusable, and be consistent about it. Keep it a pure function using only the standard library. Graders call it directly with everyday numbers in assorted shapes plus messy edge cases; they compare returned strings exactly - spacing and punctuation count - or catch an exception and read its message.
entry_contract: Implement normalize_phone(raw) taking one positional argument and returning a str; unusable input must not come back as a phone-shaped string.

hidden_spec.rule: None, non-string input, blank or whitespace-only input, or input with no digits at all raises ValueError whose message contains 'empty'.
Any alphabetic character outside a valid extension marker raises ValueError whose message contains 'letters'; never translate letters to digits.

An extension is introduced by x or ext (case-insensitive, optional dot, optional space) at the end of the input and keeps one to five digits, and it is appended to the formatted number as ', ext. NNNN'; a missing or over-long extension number raises ValueError whose message contains 'extension'.
Every non-digit character is stripped before measuring or formatting, and a ten-digit number formats exactly as (AAA) BBB-CCCC.
Eleven digits beginning with 1 are treated as a country-code prefix: drop the leading 1 and apply the ten-digit format.
Fewer than ten digits after cleanup raises ValueError whose message contains 'short'; never pad or invent missing digits.
More than eleven digits, or eleven digits that do not begin with 1, raises ValueError whose message contains 'long'.

answer_sheet.answer: None, empty, whitespace-only, or digit-free input raises ValueError 'empty'. Never a silent empty string.
Real letters outside an extension marker raise ValueError 'letters not allowed'. No vanity-number word mapping.
Marker is x or ext, case-insensitive. Keep it as ', ext. NNNN', one to five digits, else ValueError 'bad extension'.
Strip separators, then ten digits format as (AAA) BBB-CCCC. Exact punctuation - the CRM keys on it.
A leading 1 is our country code: drop it, then format the remaining digits normally.
Under the digit floor raises ValueError 'too short'. Never pad or guess missing digits.
More digits than the long form allows - or a long form without the leading 1 - raises ValueError 'too long'.
Out of scope - single-country form; no country-code table, no per-region rulebook. Only our leading-1 prefix is handled.
Out of scope - we normalize typed text; carrier, geography, and line-type lookups live in other services.

provenance.derivation: Rules derived from North American telco/form conventions (separator-stripping, ten-digit local format, optional leading country code, x/ext extensions, under/over-length rejection), not from any WiseCounsil design document.
